correctness.rationale: For the normalized quartic, six Hasse off-diagonals vanish by parity. Independent exact enumeration of all 6^4 monomial choices in F^4 reproduces the three displayed diagonal Hasse polynomials. Their pairwise differences factor as (a²+1)(c²-b²), (b²+1)(a²-c²), (c²+1)(b²-a²). Smoothness makes the first factors units, forcing three equal squares. The remaining equation factors as (s+1)²(s²+2s-1); the s=-1 case is singular, leaving two square parameters and four product-compatible signs apiece. All eight lie in F25. Direct Jacobian differentiation gives determinant 1-r at each point, hence nonzero, making the geometric zero scheme reduced etale. Frobenius swaps the two r roots independently in each sign pattern, establishing four degree-two points. The standalone exact checker enumerates all 25³ F25 triples and independently matches 8, checks the Jacobian and computes 56 F25 points per model. The algebraic factorization, rather than F25 enumeration, proves global geometric exhaustiveness.

value.rationale: The full smooth normalized Ciani family is a natural three-parameter locus of genus-three curves whose Jacobians admit three elliptic quotients. The characteristic-five superspecial degeneracy scheme is a natural arithmetic invariant, not an arbitrary finite window: its complete scheme-theoretic classification exhibits unexpected diagonal rigidity and four nonsplit quadratic closed points with no F5-marked solution. This supplies a precise reducedness/transversality and descent boundary at the first good odd characteristic beyond three. The exact invariant can guide model construction and moduli computations without requiring a downstream theorem. It is not claimed to classify all isomorphism classes or to extend to other primes.
